subject: PO vs Card: procurement process & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: PO vs Card: procurement process & next steps

Hi Sofia & Evan —

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciated the intro to the team and the clear outline of your use case (inference for patient-facing summarization pipelines). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- What we covered: Redwood hosted inference with dedicated capacity option for regulated workloads; can support VPC/private deployments later in the rollout.
- Immediate ask from your side: confirm procurement path (PO vs card), vendor onboarding requirements, and whether AWS Marketplace would be helpful for faster procurement.

Questions for you / immediate asks:
1) Which payment method does AP prefer for an initial pilot (PO, procurement card, or corporate card)?
2) Do you have a vendor onboarding packet we should complete (W-9, security questionnaire, insurance)?
3) Is there appetite to consume via AWS Marketplace (makes billing through existing cloud contracts much faster)?

Suggested next steps:
- I can share a short PO process doc and a one-pager describing the pilot configuration (attached).
- If vendor onboarding will be slow, we can do a small-value trial paid by card while the PO flows through (we often see customers use a $5k-$10k card transaction to unblock pilots).

Attachments: redwood_onepager.pdf (one-pager), Redwood_PO_Process.pdf (PO vs card flows).

I’ve looped in Aditya (SE) to help with any technical onboarding/questions. If you can share your AP contact and preferred PO template, we’ll populate a formal quote.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap. A few notes from our side after checking with AP and security: 

- AP prefers a PO for any purchase over $25,000. For smaller pilots we typically allow procurement card (P-card) purchases up to $10,000 to speed things along.
- We have a standard vendor onboarding questionnaire and require a completed W-9 and evidence of SOC2 (or relevant security questionnaire responses) before vendors are fully onboarded.
- AWS Marketplace would be ideal because it lets us charge to our existing cloud contract and reduces legal redlines; is Redwood listed there or can a listing be expedited?

I’ve attached our vendor security sheet (vendor_security_sheet.pdf) and our AP team requested a copy of your W-9 if you have one handy.

Sofia Alvarez
Sr. Program Manager, Procurement | Acme Health
sofia.alvarez@acmehealth.com

Attachments: vendor_security_sheet.pdf, company_w9.pdf

Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO vs Card: procurement process & next steps

Hi Sofia —

Appreciate the clarity — really helpful. A few quick responses and options so we can move forward this week: 

1) W-9 + SOC2: I’m attaching our standard W-9 and a link to our SOC2 report (we can provide a redacted copy if needed for security). If you’d like, I can have legal/ops send the SOC2 standard evidence pack directly to your security team.

2) Marketplace: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace; we can enable a private listing for Acme to make billing seamless. I’ll check with our marketplace ops to see what turnaround looks like (typically ~7-14 business days for private listings).

3) Pilot path to unblock quickly: If vendor onboarding will take longer than a week, we can do a short card-based pilot (we often see $5k–$7.5k pilot buys on a P-card) while AP works the PO. If a PO is required up front, we’ll prepare a formal quote and populate your PO template.

Attached: Redwood_PO_Process.pdf (explains PO vs card flows, invoicing terms). I’ve also included a DocuSign link below for quick acceptance of our pilot SOW if that helps speed legal review: https://docusign.com/na/Signing/?s=ABC123

Next steps: 
- Marissa: provide formal quote and sample invoice terms (ETA: EOD Friday)
- Aditya: will reach out to schedule a short 30-min technical onboarding to capture requirements for the pilot (seq length, expected tokens/sec, redaction needs).
- Sofia: share AP contact and preferred PO template.

Best,
Marissa

Hi team —

AP confirmed they prefer a PO for production but can approve a P-card up to $7.5k for a pilot. They need W-9 + SOC2 evidence and a formal quote to start the PO flow. Sofia also called out that AWS Marketplace would be ideal to speed procurement.

Action items for us: 
- Aditya: can you draft a short pilot quote (hosted inference pilot, up to X tokens, 30-day) with line items for dedicated capacity and hosted API options? Aim for something that can fit under $7.5k for a P-card alternative and a more scalable PO option for production.
- Laura: please flag any commercial redlines/discount flexibility (we may be asked to provide a pilot discount to fit under the P-card cap).
- Marissa: I’ll prepare the formal quote and route to Evan via Sofia; also confirm turnaround for a private AWS Marketplace listing.

I’ve attached the PO process doc we sent earlier for reference.

Thanks — let’s aim to have the quote draft by EOD today so I can push to AP.

Marissa
